items.excerpt: Meta's new terms let it crawl and train AI on advertisers' websites from October 30, 2026, as a survey found 16% of consumers grant AI data access reluctantly. Permission used to be something an advertiser or a reader gave. In the 24 hours to Saturday morning, more of it was simply written into terms, defaults and protocols by the companies that collect it, while the people asked to give it showed signs of saying yes without meaning it. The clearest case came from Meta. Its revised Commercial Terms, which take effect on October 30, 2026, add a clause to Section 1 that lets the company use automated software and test credentials to access, index, cache, copy and re-crawl websites linked to a business's products, and to use that content to train its own products. PPC Land reported on October 16 that Meta's new terms let it crawl business websites to train AI from Oct 30 , replacing a version dated March 6, 2024. Nieman Lab reporters Andrew Deck and Hanaa' Tameez first described the change on October 15. Acceptance is passive. Continued use of Meta's commercial products counts as agreement, and there is no partial opt-out. The terms do not mention robots.txt, and…

Meta yesterday published a technical account of the 2026 generation of its Generative Ads Model, known as GEM, claiming the system delivered an 18.9% conversion improvement and a 12% click-through rate improvement across its ad surfaces and objectives. Meta built one very large AI model that learns from what people do across Facebook, Instagram and its other apps, and uses it to teach the smaller models that pick which ad you see. Meta says this made people click on ads 12% more and convert 18.9% more, which matters to anyone paying for ads on those apps. A tentative schedule published on the Google Ads Developer Blog lists 25 versions between October 2026 and December 2027. Google is going to update the toolkit that software uses to talk to Google Ads twice a month instead of once a month. Most of those updates only add things, so code that already works keeps working, and the number of big updates that can break code stays at four a year. items.excerpt: You can turn off the new creative workflow… Meta started rolling out the new creative workflow in April. Also known as Multimedia Experience, it allows advertisers to provide up to 10 images and videos for a single ad. While I use and have generally been happy with the Multimedia Experience, I know I’m in the minority. Most advertisers hate it, mainly because it’s so buggy. Advertisers have had bugs both with ad creation and reporting using the breakdown by Media. What most of these advertisers don’t understand is that you don’t need to keep dealing with these bugs. You can turn this off and switch to the old way. How to Turn It Off When creating an ad, hover over the Media tooltip. There, you can click a link to “Return to original single media experience.” Even if you switch to single media, you can always hover over the same tooltip to switch back to multimedia if you want to in the future.
